scope: Additional safe classroom experiment concepts only.

experiments.title: Condensation on a cold surface
experiments.focus: Show that water vapor can turn back into liquid on a cold surface in the model.
student_observations: Tiny drops can appear on the cooler area.
Temperature affects physical change.
The substance is still water.
experiments.teacher_note: Use this as a simple link between cooling and state change.

experiments.title: Temperature and flow observation 2
experiments.focus: Show that water can behave differently when it is warmer or cooler.
student_observations: Warm and cool liquids can behave differently.
Temperature is a physical property.
The substance is still water.
experiments.teacher_note: Keep the example visual and easy to compare.

experiments.title: Stirring effect on dissolving 2
experiments.focus: Show that stirring can change how quickly a solid appears to dissolve in the model.
student_observations: The solution can change faster when stirred.
Mixing helps spread the solute through the solvent.
Rate is different from the final result.
experiments.teacher_note: Useful for talking about rate in simple language.

experiments.title: Oil and water layers 2
experiments.focus: Show that some liquids do not mix evenly and can form layers.
student_observations: The liquids can separate into layers.
Not every liquid mixes with water.
Density and miscibility are useful ideas.
experiments.teacher_note: A quick introduction to immiscible liquids.

experiments.title: Particle size effect 2
experiments.focus: Compare how different particle sizes look and behave in water.
student_observations: Some materials dissolve.
Some stay visible.
Particle size can affect the mixture.
experiments.teacher_note: Great for sorting and comparison activities.

experiments.title: Filtration and settling compare 2
experiments.focus: Compare letting particles settle with separating them by filtration.
student_observations: Solid particles can be held back by a filter.
Particles can also settle over time.
Different mixtures need different separation methods.
experiments.teacher_note: Useful as a revision activity for separation ideas.

experiments.title: Evaporation and residue 2
experiments.focus: Show that removing water can leave a solid behind from a solution.
student_observations: The liquid part can decrease.
A solid residue can remain.
Evaporation can separate some mixtures.
experiments.teacher_note: Connect with drying and salt crystals.

experiments.title: Saturation concept review 2
experiments.focus: Introduce the idea that a solution can reach a point where no more solute is easily added.
student_observations: A solution can have a limit.
More solute does not always change the result the same way.
Saturation is a useful idea for solutions.

experiments.title: Solvent choice compare 2
experiments.focus: Compare how choosing a different liquid changes whether a substance seems to dissolve or separate.
student_observations: Different liquids can behave differently as solvents.
Some substances mix well with water but not with oil.
Solvent choice matters in mixtures.

experiments.title: Density layer review 3
experiments.focus: Show that liquids can layer depending on density and miscibility.
student_observations: Liquids may separate into layers.
Density helps explain the order.
Not all liquids mix evenly.

experiments.title: Separation methods overview 4
experiments.focus: Review several ways to separate classroom mixtures.
student_observations: Some mixtures form layers.
Some mixtures can be filtered.
Some substances dissolve and need evaporation or crystallization.
